newsitem.title: USA: Gen'l Elec. may be up on new outlook - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Gen'l Elec. may be up on new outlook - Barron's.

text.p: Some market observers say that General Elecric Co's recent share price rise reflects a realization among investors that the company's outlook is changing for the better, reports Andrew Bary in the May 19 issue of Barron's.

GE rose 2 last week to 60-1/4, after hitting a record high on Thursday of 62-3/8. Barron's reports that the stock is up 21 percent for the year, following returns of 40 percent in 1996 and 45 percent in 1995.

Bary notes that GE is the main beneficiary of purchases from index funds. More importantly, there has been an increasing interest in the company on the part of institutional money and mutual fund managers who, the article said, "have underestimated the earnings power of the multinationals and overestimated the profit potential of smaller stocks".

The article cites Nick Heymann, analyst at Natwest Securities, who says that GE will benefit from several factors, namely a quality assurance program that could save billions by 2000, a shift towards the high-margin service business, and growing sales abroad.
Heymann believes that profits per share over the next few years could rise at a 15 percent to 17 percent rate, against Wall Street estimates of 12 percent to 13 percent, the article said.
Heymann says GE could earn more than $4 in 2000, and that its stock could top 100.
The article said that others discount GE's rise as being part of the craze for "Nifty-Fifty" issues, and that much of its popularity stems from the "cult status" of its chief executive, Jack Welch.
